image_description: A close-up view of a grey whale's head and upper torso emerging vertically from the ocean surface. The whale displays characteristic mottled dark grey skin with extensive white patches (barnacles and cyamids). The rostrum is arched, and the blowholes are visible at the apex. The background consists of calm, greenish-blue sea water and a distant horizon line.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the distinctive arched rostrum and the blowhole area at the top of the head, matching the anatomical description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture exhibits the classic mottled pattern with high-contrast white callosities/barnacle clusters typical of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image frame cuts off at the shoulder/neck region; the posterior back where dorsal knuckles would be located is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior portion of the body is visible; the full spindle shape cannot be verified due to cropping and submersion.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint, the visible body section confirms the mottled grey and white patch coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are located further down the body and are completely submerged/out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: High-resolution details on the head show the rough, bumpy texture associated with callosities and barnacle attachments.
